authority: the CM1 r21.1 release source (base.F, init3d.F, param.F)
driver: the CM1 differential oracle of the development repository (not distributed): CM1 r21.1 built from the release and GM1 run on the same deck
horizon: model time zero. Initialization is the one part of the model whose correctness needs no trajectory: the initial state either is CM1's or it is not, and the difference is visible before a single step. Both sides therefore stop before stepping, which also makes the whole comparison GPU-free.
purpose: Per-selector record of what has and has not been checked against CM1 r21.1. A value whose status is not 'validated' is reported as UNVALIDATED in every run receipt that selects it and in gpuwm-cm1 doctor.

integration.admission: admitted for a run (the control for ibalance = 2: the same warm bubble without the balance)
integration.method: the first 15 minutes, output every minute, GM1 on an RTX 4090 against CM1 r21.1 (CPU), both on Morrison (GM1 morrison-mp10, CM1 ptype = 5) at eqtset = 2 (the oracle's integration vs cm1 driver --like-for-like); pass: w nrmsd <= 0.02 to 300 s and <= 0.10 to 900 s, max w ratio 0.97-1.03 where CM1's max w >= 1 m/s, theta' nrmsd <= 0.02

7.method: differential against the real CM1 r21.1 binary at model time zero: both sides build the same deck and stop before a single step (CM1 writes its initial output time, GM1 runs initialization.iconly = 1), and the published frames are compared field by field by cm1core.oracle.compare; cases 'iinit-7' (32 x 32 km, 1 km) and 'iinit-7-500km' (100 x 100 cells of 5 km, where the warm core passes 0.1 K and takes init3d.F:1250's random noise), fields th3d,u3d,v3d,prs,rho,qv, iorigin = 2, random_generator = "cm1": the vortex, its gradient-wind pressure and its noise are CM1's word for word (max |GM1-CM1| = 0 in every field)

8.method: differential against the real CM1 r21.1 binary at model time zero: both sides build the same deck and stop before a single step (CM1 writes its initial output time, GM1 runs initialization.iconly = 1), and the published frames are compared field by field by cm1core.oracle.compare; case 'iinit-8', field th3d, checked as a BOUND rather than a norm: init3d.F:1277 adds amplitude*(2*rand-1) inside the thermal, so the two sides cannot agree word for word there. max|GM1-CM1| = 0.396 K against the 2*amplitude = 0.4 K bound, and the field is identical outside the thermal, so the deterministic envelope -- placement, radii, shape and amplitude -- is what is confirmed.
8.not_checked: the random component of init3d.F:1257-1296's line thermal. CM1 adds amplitude*(2*rand-1) inside the thermal from gfortran's generator, and GM1 draws from its own; the two fields differ everywhere inside the thermal even when everything else is identical. What IS confirmed is the deterministic envelope -- placement, radii, shape and amplitude -- as a bound: max|GM1-CM1| stays under 2*amplitude inside the thermal and is exactly zero outside it. See irandp=1 for the same limitation. With random_generator = "cm1" (the importer's default for a CM1 namelist) the noise is CM1's word for word: see the row "8:cm1".

8:cm1.method: differential against the real CM1 r21.1 binary at model time zero: both sides build the same deck and stop before a single step (CM1 writes its initial output time, GM1 runs initialization.iconly = 1), and the published frames are compared field by field by cm1core.oracle.compare; case 'iinit-8-cm1-stream', fields th3d with initialization.random_generator = "cm1": libgfortran's xoshiro256** random_number, seeded as init3d.F:427-440 seeds it, so the thermal's random noise is CM1's word for word (max |GM1-CM1| = 0.0 K); and case 'iinit-8-cm1-words' (CM1's stock grid, no words declared)

0.method: identity: irandp=0 adds nothing, so the field is whatever the iinit arm built, and every iinit case above ran with it

1.method: structure and reproducibility only, in rust/cm1-state/src/initial_perturbation.rs: CM1's traversal order, CM1's draw count per global point including the margin cells, CM1's amplitude and depth limit per testcase, a zero mean, the variance of a uniform on [-A,A], bit reproducibility from one seed, and a different field from a different seed
1.not_checked: init3d.F:427-440 seeds gfortran's random_number; its sequence is a property of one libgfortran build, not of CM1, and GM1 declares its own generator (splitmix64/top24-binary32) and its own recorded seed. A word-for-word differential is impossible by construction. What is checked instead, in rust/cm1-state/src/initial_perturbation.rs, is everything about the field that is not the numbers: CM1's traversal order, CM1's draw count per global point including the margin cells, CM1's amplitude and depth limit per testcase, a zero mean, the variance of a uniform on [-A,A], bit reproducibility from one seed and a different field from a different seed. With random_generator = "cm1" (the importer's default for a CM1 namelist) the field is CM1's word for word: see the row "1:cm1". GM1's own stream also walks one more row and column than CM1's testcase-0 loop (jj = 0..ny+3 against 0..ny+2) and centres them one cell further out; it is kept so every seeded run recorded before keeps its field.

1:cm1.method: differential against the real CM1 r21.1 binary at model time zero: both sides build the same deck and stop before a single step (CM1 writes its initial output time, GM1 runs initialization.iconly = 1), and the published frames are compared field by field by cm1core.oracle.compare; case 'irandp-1-cm1-stream', fields th3d with initialization.random_generator = "cm1" and CM1's own traversal (jj = 0..ny+2, two draws per point, init3d.F:1459-1482): the field is CM1's word for word (max |GM1-CM1| = 0.0 K)
